findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is used here with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this implementation applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the model’s datetime value. Those functions require a number, so building cursors for non-empty audit-log results raises `TypeError` and the optimized request fails. It also returns the raw numeric cursor from `value_from_cursor`, rather than converting it to a datetime for the queryset filter. Reuse the datetime-specific conversion and key logic from `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Negative offsets cause an error in Django queryset slicing
findings.body: This branch deliberately passes a negative start offset to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but Django querysets reject negative slice indices and raise `ValueError`; they do not interpret them as a way to paginate backwards. A request with a negative cursor offset therefore fails instead of returning a page. The non-advanced previous-page path can hit the same invalid slice when its cursor offset is negative.
